en: The heroes spoke these words,
The great men spoke these words.
The hero leapt up and ran,
His door-sized legs bending,
Bustling about, they took the horses,
Their swiftness could not be distinguished.
With a clatter they stepped quickly,
Opening the door, they rejoiced.
Ebeche stood amazed,
They were the ones who waited upon the khan,
Who stayed in the khan's presence,
Who had witnessed many wonders,
Among the people into whom they were born,
The valiant men performed their service.
Their deeds and their courage,
All were the equals of a khan.
Their spirit, wisdom, and skill,
When God granted heroes to the land,
He himself went wheeling around,
The young warrior was passing beyond his limit,
Saying the horse fled like Joomart,
Roaring, he appealed to God,
He was both a hero and a giant,
Throughout the eighteen thousand worlds,
The hero’s trail was deep,
Saying that giant Joomart had come,
It was a true battle cry to the multitude,
Saying that God himself had bestowed him,
They came gathering together, it is said,
Where was he while going about the encirclement!
Like a target forty arm-spans wide,
They clashed and grappled with one another.
There was no ground spacious enough for the hero,
Gnawed at his own bit,
Pierced the blue heights and tore through them,
All twelve groaned aloud.
When he went to Perizat,
You ordered him to go quickly,
Shamdarkhan,
When he mounted the steed Kulansur,
From Denebay’s sleeve,
Its flame enveloped the mountain,
The blue-maned horse, the swift gray racer,
The turmoil of the commotion,
We spread across the face of the earth,
The noble stood upon the battlefield,
We came for his feat of valor.
Mount Kulansur and set out,
Wheeling around, they confronted one another,
The soul became sated with delight,
The champion had mastered himself,
You yourself had set it in place.
They came one by one from the very root,
The children of humankind make it so,
From a sorrowful heart they make a feast.
Courage befits a man,
He is parted from his people and homeland,
He demands it and lays claim to the property,
If he says, “Give it,” there is one God.
A lean one may be found among them all,
The mortal who said he would not give,
Restless in this fleeting world,
He makes him close his eyes and takes him.
Stormy-eyed Lady Aikanim,
Having remained without thinking, [?],
Hearing the elder sister’s tidings,
The dark-haired boy would stand,
Bloodthirsty Manas would stand.
Of the people as vast as the whole world, [?],
The youngest child of your father Shoo,
A mortal created by God,
Where no outsider had ever come,
He had not inclined himself to forgiveness,
None remained who did not draw back,
The more he perceived, the more he understood,
Stirred to his very foundations, he surged,
The more he pondered, the more he thought,
The longer he stayed, the more mature he became,
His bearing was filled with surging blood,
Stirring him to the core and making him ready,
When told to go and take it, he struck freely,
When told to come quickly, he arrived straightaway,
When told to fetch water, he crossed [?],
From drinking down to the dregs,
God had ordained him from his very root,
His core was tempered more sharply than a cart’s iron,
The warrior was roused by blood,
Draped in a black caparison,
Of the noble hero Manas,
The black caparison was fastened,
Of the bloodthirsty hero Semetey,
This horse of his that had turned away,
Was turned by the fierce hero Seytek!
From among the valiant men,
The son of Er-Köbösh,
He became a champion sent by God.
He decreed punishment for Manas,
Rise up and take him captive,
Until there was respite from this hero,
Would any maiden he had carried off remain?
The Creator, my God,
Wishing to behold his bliss,
To the far side, Lady Aikanim,
Not a person beyond remained,
The star in the sky was pale,
Manas was a champion like a thoroughbred,
He was Akköbük’s friend,
At his very root he was a khan,
A solemn pledge handed down from the forefathers,
If a girl as beautiful as the moon appeared,
For the lineage of the warrior-champion,
When the time came, she was given,
There was such a promise,
He would ponder upon seeing the star,
If the hero’s spirit were troubled,
He was an indomitable hero,
Manas descended for his child,
Manas was delivered to the khan,
Sending the child to his friend,
Taking up his blood-smeared sword,
How shall I tighten the saddle?
If God wills, taking up the keen blade,
He turned back from the lean horse,
We shall harness the swift horse,
Wishing to see what his horse was like,
Sultan Aikan,
Turning his horse, saying he would stay as a guest,
Gathering together on a hill,
Saying, “Now fate will be decided,”
If the lion’s destiny permits, they will meet,
If they unite and come as a company,
Slay him, brave warrior, valiant fighter,
One who seeks a quarrel with the enemy,
Demand treasure and livestock,
On hearing the news, we were struck down,
To deliver news worthy of a mighty one,
I grieved for Bek Kambar,
He prevailed, driving back the enemy,
He disturbed the servant’s sleep,
There was no need to enter among them, father,
He drew the red spear,
He drew blood from the brave warrior,
Striking resoundingly, he took a solitary life,
After enduring so much hardship,
He went to three places,
Two spirits appeared before his eyes,
Aikan, swift as water upon his horse,
If he brought him in his grasp,
The mighty hero Kenen,
I shall cast him down and take him,
If no enemy who struck us comes,
They fought and dealt such blows,
His home was in Salmak,
A wolf among those who remained.
By the might of His power,
Strengthened by the spirits’ breath,
From the khoja in the white turban,
From the mullah who recited for the marriage,
From words eloquently spoken before the crowd,
From the honored one who knew the rite,
Reciting the Quran and declaring the marriage bond,
Gathering the property of the ancestral spirits,
Those speaking after you were pleased,
For three days the people would not part,
She became like a red-belted moon,
His mother Kogoy, invoking two spirits,
Cursing his fate, there was no tomorrow,
The shrine of the Ubai people,
Asking forgiveness, he prepared the road,
To the shrine where the sacrifice was made,
When he performed the dawn prayer,
Seytek turned toward the righteous road,
From Kalyk, who brought the news,
I said, “I shall shed blood,”
Running from snare to snare,
Returning together to the honored road,
A proud soul went on.
My kinsman,
For me, the place of honor in the house feels strange,
By Kurmanjan’s dignity,
My face was troubled from the outset,
Having seen what was tempered in this world,
Without dismounting from the horse in this world,
Crossing mountain passes on countless journeys,
My honor, esteemed more highly than a khan,
My words that fill the mouth,
Each surpassing the other,
He would ride through the five peoples,
The valleys and all the forty peoples,
Taking his place and reaching the very root,
When daylight appeared as night,
Displaying much of his imposing might,
The village and the river joined together,
The two enter separate houses,
His two elder brothers died quickly,
Ak Joldoy and Saikal, my two elder brothers,
Saying that Akba turned his neck,
Making a pure wish, he set out,
Saying that the venerable elder did it,
Kinsmen with the komuz,
Ruining it with precious things,
Setting out toward the [?],
My brow was destined to be seen,
Being broken apart with the soldiers,
My kinsman together with my Balka,
Ninety wrestler kinsmen,
They met beside the Jaiyk,
Having dug an equal share from the sea,
One who did not shrink from the nobles,
Digging out iron by the thousands,
The moonlit, verdant lands,
Begin together with us,
Having it pierced like a reed,
The hearts of a thousand poured forth,
The mouth that feared for life,
A living soul went on without dying,
Becoming an iron core,
The blood that would not flow turned aside,
From the seven kinds of this futile world,
Is there a soul that never grows weary?
Why did the orphaned day turn away,
My two elder brothers began their journey,
The whole world is bare,
He looked back and left it behind.
The Chük grave blossomed and grew,
He would pass them by the thousands,
He does not see what was carved from stone,
He destroyed it, making it fit for digging,
Having the tomb built of stone,
My generous lord was laid to rest,
The nomadic people fell into sorrow,
Saying, “My father left without doing it,”
Saying that he passed from both worlds,
Black strength lay out on the steppe,
Kulakchy and my Küchügüm,
My strength, trained for battle,
Having gone and stayed at the summer pasture,
Having cut all his sleeves,
If what was said about me is true,
Saying, “Give it yourself from the giant,”
Now the strength would proceed,
When he said so, they obeyed.
Returning from the emir into his hands,
Kösöy and Koshoy led the way,
Appearing before his people,
Among the many elders, [?],
Setting up a khanate at Kara-Suu,
Settling upon the supporting height of Olok,
Esen and Koshoy awaited the hero,
Amassing countless stores of wealth,
Arranging it with Kökül,
All of the forty companions,
Sated them with abundant gold and property,
Each time they assembled at their dwelling,
His nature became known among the people,
He became renowned throughout the land,
